chapters.n: Fourth Nephi covers nearly 300 years in one chapter. It opens right after Christ’s visit: the disciples have established the church everywhere, and all who truly repent are baptized and receive the Holy Ghost.

f.g: Counted from the sign of Christ’s birth; Christ visited in this year.

chapters.n: By the 36th year everyone — Nephites and Lamanites alike — is converted. There are no arguments, and everyone treats others fairly.
They share everything, so there are no rich or poor, no slaves or free. All are free and share in the “heavenly gift.” This is a true Zion society.

f.g: Sharing in the Holy Ghost and the blessings of the gospel.

chapters.n: The 37th year passes in continued peace.
Christ’s disciples perform great miracles — healing the sick, raising the dead, restoring sight and hearing — always and only in Jesus’ name.
Year after year passes in peace, up to the 59th year. Mormon’s quick listing of years suggests how uneventful — in a good way — those decades were.
The Lord blesses them so richly that they rebuild cities that had been burned in the great destruction.
Even the great city of Zarahemla is rebuilt.
Some cities had sunk and been covered by water during the destruction, so they could never be rebuilt.
The people grow strong and numerous and become “fair and delightsome” — a description of their righteousness, prosperity, and joy.

f.g: Pleasing and beautiful, especially in their way of life.

chapters.n: They marry and raise families, and God blesses them with all the promises he had made. Ordinary family life flourishes in righteousness.
They no longer follow the rituals of the law of Moses, which Christ had fulfilled, but follow his commandments — fasting, praying, and meeting often to pray and hear the word.
There is no contention anywhere, and the disciples perform mighty miracles.
A century passes. All of Christ’s original twelve have died and gone to paradise except the three who remain on earth; others are ordained to replace them.

f.w: save it were the three who should tarry

chapters.n: Here is the secret of their peace: the love of God dwells in their hearts. Unity grows from within, not from rules.
There is no envy, strife, unrest, immorality, lying, or murder. Mormon concludes there could not be a happier people anywhere God ever created.

f.w: there could not be a happier people

chapters.n: No robbers, no murderers, and no more “Lamanites” or other “-ites” — no tribal labels at all. They are one people, the children of Christ.

f.g: Group labels such as Nephites, Lamanites, Zoramites.

chapters.n: Mormon exclaims how blessed they were! They prosper in everything for 110 years, and the first generation after Christ passes away still in peace.
Nephi, the chief disciple and record keeper, dies, and his son Amos takes over the record on the plates of Nephi.
Amos keeps the record 84 years. Peace mostly continues, but a small group revolts from the church and takes the name Lamanites again — the first crack in Zion.
Amos dies 194 years after Christ, and his son, also named Amos, continues the record, which Mormon calls the book of Nephi — this book.
Two hundred years have passed; almost everyone of the second generation has died.
Mormon notes that the people spread across the land and became extremely rich because of their prosperity in Christ. Blessings bring a test.
In the 201st year pride appears — expensive clothing, pearls, and fine worldly things. This is how Zion begins to fall: not with a war but with vanity.
From then on they stop sharing their goods. The economic equality that marked Zion ends.
They divide into social classes and build churches to make money, denying Christ’s true church. Class division and religion-for-profit go together.
By 210 years there are many churches claiming Christ but denying most of his gospel. They accept all kinds of wickedness and give sacred ordinances to those forbidden because of unworthiness.
This corrupt church grows rapidly because of wickedness and Satan’s hold on people’s hearts.
Another church openly denies Christ and persecutes the true church for its humility and faith, despising them for their miracles.
These persecutors imprison the three disciples who remained, but by the power of God’s word the prisons split open, and the disciples go on working miracles.

f.w: the prisons were rent in twain

chapters.n: Despite the miracles, the people harden their hearts and try to kill the disciples, just as Jerusalem sought to kill Jesus.
They throw the disciples into furnaces, but they emerge unharmed.
They throw them into dens of wild beasts, but the disciples play with the beasts like a child with a lamb and come out unharmed.

Still the people harden their hearts, led by priests and false prophets to build churches and commit sin. They strike the followers of Jesus, who do not strike back. Wickedness deepens year after year until the 230th year.
In the 231st year there is a great division among the people.
A group arises called Nephites, who are true believers in Christ; the old family names — Jacobites, Josephites, Zoramites — return among them.
The true believers, including the three disciples who remained, are called by these names. The labels are back, though here they mark faithfulness.

Those who reject the gospel are called Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites. Mormon stresses they did not simply drift into unbelief — they willfully rebelled, and taught their children not to believe.
This rebellion comes from the wickedness of their fathers, just as in the beginning. They are taught to hate God’s children, as the early Lamanites were taught to hate Nephi’s descendants.
By 244 years, the wicked have grown strong and far outnumber God’s people.
They keep building churches for themselves and decorating them with precious things. Decades pass — 250, then 260 years.

f.w: adorn them with all manner of precious things

chapters.n: The wicked revive the secret oaths and combinations of the Gadianton robbers — organized crime and conspiracy return.
Even the people called Nephites grow proud because of their riches and become as vain as the Lamanites. Now no group is safe from pride.
From this time on the disciples begin to sorrow for the sins of the world — fulfilling the sorrow Christ said the three would feel.

f.w: sorrow for the sins of the world

chapters.n: By 300 years, Nephites and Lamanites alike are extremely wicked. The golden age is completely gone.
Gadianton robbers spread over the land, and only the disciples of Jesus remain righteous. The people hoard gold and silver and engage in every kind of trade.
After 305 years Amos dies, and his brother Ammaron takes over the record.
In the 320th year, Ammaron, prompted by the Holy Ghost, hides all the sacred records handed down through generations.
He hides them “unto the Lord” so they can return to the remnant of Jacob as prophesied. This ends Ammaron’s record and sets up young Mormon’s story.

f.w: come again unto the remnant of the house of Jacob
